title: Levi Saba

paragraphs: In [Eruvin 97b (Hyman cites 97)](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.97b.8) and [Chullin 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.29b.3), Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish spoke in his name. In the [Jerusalem Talmud, Eruvin 10:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.10.2.3), the reading is Levi Sukhia; likewise [there, 10:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.10.12.3), Shimon ben Lakish in the name of Levi Sikhiyya; and [Yoma 8:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yoma.8.6.5) has Rabbi Shimon [ben Lakish] in the name of Rabbi Levi Sikhiyya.[^2]
In [Pesachim 6:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.6.1.18), Shimon ben Lakish speaks in the name of Rabbi Sukhia; Hyman suggests that the name Levi dropped out.[^1]

notes.text: The linked Yerushalmi gives Sukhia in Eruvin 10:2, Sovaya in 10:12, and Sukhiyya in Yoma 8:6. The Yoma text gives Shimon without a patronymic. Pesachim reads Rabbi Sovaya without Levi. Hyman suggests that Levi dropped out.
[Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2332&lang=en) points to Eruvin 97b and Chullin 29b, both of which give Resh Lakish speaking in the name of Levi the Elder.
